title: Finding organization by subquestion (foundational)
description: Findings are grouped under the subquestions that produced them, in the mission's dependency order. Organization by subquestion keeps the report's structure aligned with how the investigation actually ran. Each group opens with its one-line answer, then the supporting detail. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Research Report Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Citation insertion from evidence links (foundational)
description: Every factual sentence in the draft gets its citation inserted from the evidence links recorded during the investigation. Sentences with no link are flagged for the auditor instead of being published uncited. Citation insertion is mechanical and complete: no claim the evidence supports goes without its marker. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Unresolved-question tracking (foundational)
description: Subquestions that remain unanswered get their own report section with what was tried and why it fell short. Unresolved questions are first-class report content, not buried in a footnote, because they define the next investigation. Each one carries the negative-result summary from the analyzer. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Research Report Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Evidence summarization per section (foundational)
description: Each report section opens with a two-sentence evidence summary: what was found and how strong the support is. Summaries are extractive, built from the top-scoring evidence passages, so they never drift from the sources. The summary lets busy readers get the point without reading every citation. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Research Report Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Report assembly and completeness check (foundational)
description: Assembly stitches sections, citations, summaries, and unresolved questions into the final document, then runs a completeness check: every subquestion appears exactly once, every factual sentence has a citation, and the unresolved section is non-empty when gaps exist. A report that fails the check goes back for repair instead of shipping incomplete. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Automatic Research Report Builder practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
